llm_judge_report.task_name: Prepare two hamburgers and a salad

relevance.justification: All messages were strictly focused on task execution, sharing capabilities, and addressing current workstation statuses.

clarity.justification: Messages were generally unambiguous and easy to interpret, clearly stating locations, intentions, and requests.

grounding.justification: There were grounding errors: Robot_2 claimed to be holding lettuce at t=13s when it was actually holding a knife (revealed at t=21s), and Robot_3 failed to recognize a patty was already cooked at t=21s.

coordination_utility.justification: Communication failed to prevent deadlocks. Robot_3 continuously locked the Stove by spamming COOK, which prevented Robot_1 from dropping the meat patty at t=18s, and they never resolved this conflict.

redundancy.justification: Robot_3 exhibited severe repetition, broadcasting almost the exact same failure message about the missing meat patty at t=10s, 12s, 16s, 34s, and 45s.

planning_coherence.justification: Plans were poorly coordinated: Robot_3 spammed COOK before ingredients were dropped, Robot_1 attempted to COOK without the skill, and Robot_2 struggled with capacity limits and cutting already-cut items.

failure_explanation_quality.justification: Robot_3 clearly articulated the missing ingredient error but failed to diagnose the workstation lock preventing Robot_1's drop. Robot_2 misdiagnosed its CUT failure by hallucinating its inventory.

llm_judge_report.overall_summary: Although communication was on-topic and clearly phrased, the team suffered from repetitive chatter, ungrounded inventory claims, and an inability to resolve workstation locks, resulting in very poor task progress.
